summary: Orbital/space-based compute is becoming increasingly real and is underappreciated by public markets
summary_extended: Baker argues that orbital/space-based compute is transitioning from science fiction to a credible near-term infrastructure category, and that public markets are not pricing this possibility at all. He visited Starbase and came away with increased conviction, noting that 'orbital compute feels more real every day.' A key data point is that Benchmark — a top-tier VC firm with no particular ideological alignment to the Elon Musk ecosystem — independently funded Star Cloud, an orbital compute startup that is partnering with SpaceX to leverage Starlink's inter-satellite laser communication technology, which Baker views as the critical enabling infrastructure for low-latency orbital compute. Baker treats Benchmark's involvement as an independent sanity check validating the thesis beyond SpaceX boosterism, and frames this as a potential entirely new category of AI infrastructure that is absent from any current public market estimates or sell-side models.
